hook.text: Espresso uses 9 bars of pressure—nine times atmospheric pressure—to force water through finely ground coffee.

buildup.text: That pressure extracts in 25 seconds what drip takes 4 minutes to achieve. Speed changes everything.

discovery.text: Pressure emulsifies coffee oils and creates crema—the golden foam on top that traps aromatic compounds.

twist.text: Too much pressure causes channeling: water finds weak spots in the puck and over-extracts them.

climax.text: Dialing in espresso means adjusting grind, dose, and time until pressure creates a balanced shot.

punchline.text: Nine bars, 25 seconds, one perfect shot. Pressure is the secret.

quiz.question: How much pressure does a standard espresso machine use?
